html:
A culture of walled towns south of Lake Chad, in today's Chad, Cameroon and Nigeria, known from about the middle of the first millennium BCE until the 16th century CE.

Its people made terracotta figures of humans and animals, bronze ornaments and large burial jars, and lived on mounds above the floodplains of the Chari and Logone rivers. Legends of the region speak of the Sao as giants. They were pressed and finally absorbed by Kanem-Bornu under rulers such as Idris Alooma; their descendants are thought to include the Kotoko people of the river towns. Its objects are in museums in N'Djamena and abroad.
sum: A culture of walled towns south of Lake Chad, in today's Chad, Cameroon and Nigeria, known from about the middle of the first millennium BCE until the 16th century CE.
